chunks: Muhammad ibn ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'So-and-so conveys the greetings to you, and so-and-so, and so-and-so.' He said, 'And the greetings be upon them.' I said, 'They are asking you for supplication.' He said, 'And what is the matter with them?' I said, 'Abu Ja'far has imprisoned them.' He said, 'And what is the matter with them and with him?' I said, 'He employed them, and he imprisoned them.' He said, 'And what is the matter with them and with him? Did I not forbid them? Did I not forbid them? Did I not forbid them? They are of the Fire, they are of the Fire, they are of the Fire.' He said, 'Then he said: O Allah, deceive their Sultan from them.' I said, 'So I departed from Makkah and asked about them, and behold, they had been released after this speech by three days.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about those imprisoned by the Caliph who were employed by him?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s discernment regarding the political compromises of his contemporaries, specifically those who served under the Abbasid Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur. By repeatedly asking 'What is with them?' and declaring them 'of the Fire,' Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the spiritual danger of legitimizing unjust authority, a core theme in Shia political theology. The immediate fulfillment of his prayer for the Sultan to be 'deceived' (khada') serves as a divine validation of his authority and the transient nature of worldly power.
